goal: The admin's Products list, Customers list and the platform's Stores list each read and send one page of 100 with a count and a next page, and the Products list reads only what it shows.
why: Today the Products list sends every product of the store (about 0.9 KB each, no limit) and runs 16 or more statements, the Customers list builds heavy aggregates over every order before it cuts to 100, and the Stores list loads every store. After: 100 rows a page, 'N of total' on each list, and 5 statements or fewer for the Products list.

commits.title: The Products list reads its categories and a count, not the whole editor context

changes.how: Add `export async function countProductsNeedingMeasure(storeId: string): Promise<number>`, read through typedRow()/typedRows() with `z.object({ n: col.int })` (src/server/typed-rows.ts). One statement: `select case when not exists (select 1 from commerce.products p where p.store_id = $1 and p.sold_by_measure) and not exists (select 1 from commerce.terms t where t.store_id = $1 and t.requires_unit_price) then 0 else (select count(*)::int from commerce.products p where p.store_id = $1 and p.status = 'active' and p.kind = 'goods' and commerce.unit_price_required(p.store_id, p.id) and exists (select 1 from commerce.product_variants v where v.store_id = p.store_id and v.product_id = p.id and v.active and v.delivery = 'physical' and v.measure_amount is null)) end as n`. The inner conditions are exactly productsNeedingMeasure()'s (same file, lines 61 to 91): the `exists` on variants replaces its `q.skus is not null`. Do not change productsNeedingMeasure().

In each case that calls productsNeedingMeasure(), add `expect(await countProductsNeedingMeasure(storeId)).toBe((await productsNeedingMeasure(storeId, locale)).length)` with that case's own arguments, including the case where a category is marked after products were assigned and a store with nothing marked (expects 0).

In ProductList's Promise.all: (1) replace `archived ? Promise.resolve([]) : productsNeedingMeasure(...)` by two values: `needingCount = archived || needsFilter ? 0 : await countProductsNeedingMeasure(store.id)` and `needing = needsFilter ? await productsNeedingMeasure(store.id, store.localization.locales[0] ?? locale) : []` (both inside the Promise.all as promises). (2) Replace `canWrite && !needsFilter ? getEditorContext(store) : Promise.resolve(null)` by `canWrite && !needsFilter ? listTerms({ storeId: store.id, contentType: "product" }) : Promise.resolve(null)` (import listTerms from '@/server/taxonomy'; this is the same call getEditorContext() makes at src/server/products.ts line 140). (3) Build `bulk` when that terms value is not null: `terms: terms.map((t) => ({ id: t.id, name: t.name, kind: t.kind }))` and `markets: store.markets.map((m) => ({ code: m.code, name: m.name, currency: m.currency }))`. (4) `<NeedsContentNotice count={needingCount} …>` and the tab's condition `(needingCount > 0 || needsFilter)`; `<NeedsContentList products={needing} …>` unchanged. Remove the getEditorContext import. Leave getEditorContext() itself alone: the product editor needs it.

commits.title: The Customers list picks its 100 people before it adds up their orders, and says how many there are

changes.how: Keep listCustomers()'s signature and row shape; add an `offset?: number` option (default 0) and a second export `countCustomers(storeId, { q, tag })`. Restructure the one statement so the cut happens before the heavy aggregates. Keep the CTEs `bought` and `accounts` as they are. Replace `by_email` by a light one, `seen as (select email, max(placed_at) as last_order, min(placed_at) as first_order from bought group by email)`. Add `picked as (select coalesce(a.email, s.email) as email, a.id as customer_id, a.name as account_name, a.avatar_path, a.verified, a.created_at, s.last_order, s.first_order from accounts a full join seen s on s.email = a.email where <the search condition> and <the tag condition> order by coalesce(s.last_order, a.created_at) desc nulls last limit ${limit} offset ${offset})`. The search condition today also matches the name from the newest order; keep that by adding to `seen` the column `(array_agg(name order by placed_at desc) filter (where name is not null))[1] as name` (one more light aggregate) and searching `lower(coalesce(a.name, s.name, ''))`. Then compute, joined to `picked` only: by_email (count(*), latest_order by array_agg) `from bought b join picked p on p.email = b.email group by b.email`; `spent` the same way; `subs` with `where … and lower(coalesce(c.email, s.email)) in (select email from picked)`. The final select reads from picked left join these three, in picked's order (repeat the order by). countCustomers() is `with bought …, accounts …, seen … select count(*)::int as n from accounts a full join seen s on s.email = a.email where <search> and <tag>`, read through typedRow(). The privacy conditions inside `bought` (restricted_at is null, anonymised_at is null, the `${bought}` status fragment) must stay word for word.

Read `page` from the query as the Products page does; call `listCustomers(store.id, { q, tag, offset: (page - 1) * 100 })` and `countCustomers(store.id, { q, tag })` in the existing Promise.all; under the table draw fillWords(words.shownOf, { shown, total }) when total > customers.length and previous/next links that keep q and tag. Add to src/lib/admin-messages/customers.en.ts `list`: shownOf '{shown} of {total}', next 'Next 100 customers', previous 'Previous 100 customers'; and to customers.nb.ts: '{shown} av {total}', 'Neste 100 kunder', 'Forrige 100 kunder'.

Add a case 'a store with 150 customers lists 100 and counts 150': insert 150 rows into commerce.customers for a fresh store (insert … select from generate_series, distinct emails), 10 of them with one paid order each through the file's own order helper; expect listCustomers(storeId) length 100, countCustomers(storeId) 150, listCustomers(storeId, { offset: 100 }) length 50 with no email in both pages, and that a customer with an order has orders 1 and the right spentMinor. The existing cases (line 95 on) must pass unchanged.
